issue: Flask class mixes many responsibilities (WSGI handling, CLI registration, static file serving, request processing) in a single class spanning the whole file
why_it_matters: makes the code hard to understand, changes in one area risk breaking unrelated behavior, and hampers isolated testing
suggested_refactor: Extract request handling, static file serving, and CLI command registration into separate helper classes or modules, leaving Flask as a thin orchestrator

issue: wsgi_app method contains deeply nested try/except blocks and manages context, error handling, and debug logic all together
why_it_matters: high nesting reduces readability and increases chance of bugs; splitting responsibilities would simplify maintenance
suggested_refactor: Move error handling and debug‑only logic to dedicated private methods, keeping wsgi_app focused on delegating to request_context

issue: Several imports at the top of the file (e.g., collections.abc as cabc, inspect, os, sys, typing as t, weakref, urllib.parse modules) are never referenced in the module
why_it_matters: dead imports increase import time and obscure which dependencies are actually needed, making future refactors riskier
suggested_refactor: Remove imports that are not used; run a linter to verify unused symbols and delete them

issue: default_config dictionary hard‑codes many Flask configuration values (e.g., DEBUG, TESTING, SESSION_COOKIE_NAME) directly in code
why_it_matters: embedding defaults makes it harder for deployments to override settings without editing source, reducing flexibility
suggested_refactor: Move default configuration values to a separate configuration file or environment‑driven defaults and load them at runtime

issue: QuerySet class spans over 1800 lines and implements countless database operations, iteration protocols, bulk actions, and async helpers, violating single‑responsibility principle
why_it_matters: the monolithic design makes comprehension difficult, impedes isolated testing, and increases risk of regressions when modifying a single method
suggested_refactor: Split QuerySet into smaller composable classes (e.g., QueryBuilder, BulkOperations, AsyncHelpers) and delegate responsibilities accordingly

issue: Both bulk_create (lines 890‑894) and bulk_update (lines 1023‑1025) validate that batch_size is a positive integer with identical code
why_it_matters: duplicate validation logic can diverge in the future, causing inconsistent error handling
suggested_refactor: Introduce a private helper _validate_positive_batch_size(batch_size) and call it from both methods

issue: BaseIterable._async_generator creates a new thread‑to‑sync bridge for each chunk, adding overhead especially for large result sets
why_it_matters: the extra thread switches may degrade throughput; profiling could confirm impact on large queries
suggested_refactor: Consider using a pure async iterator implementation or batch‑fetching without crossing sync‑async boundaries; profile to quantify cost

issue: MAX_GET_RESULTS constant is set to the magic number 21, limiting the number of rows fetched for get() calls
why_it_matters: hard‑coding limits flexibility and may need adjustment for different backends; changes require source edits
suggested_refactor: Expose the limit via a configurable setting or parameter, and document its purpose; avoid magic numbers
